reviews.text: It's alright. Good performances and solid cautionary druglord tale. I held off on it for so long due to the types of dudes I knew growing up that loved this film. Yeah, it's definitely a tough guy film. I can appreciate Al Pacino and Michelle Pfeiffer's performances though. While watching, I kept thinking back to my highschool weed dealer/friend who had a poster of the film on the wall of his totally blacklit room next to the iguana enclosure. I wonder how he's doing.

I don’t know about this one. I imagine it’s supposed to be a classic film and be awesome but it just wasn’t. The plot was a little unclear to me because of everyone having an accent, call me racist but I genuinely did not know what was happening. That probably played a role in why I didn’t like the movie as much to be honest. I don’t really know how to categorize this movie because if you treat it as an action movie, there wasn’t a lot of it and it was mostly gun fights. If you treat as more of a story driven movie, I have to be honest it wasn’t awesome because it was just drug-slop. Tony was also one of the least like-able main character in a movie I’ve genuinely seen. He’s just unstable and rude for like no reason, midway through I was genuinely wondering if I was supposed to be rooting for this guy. Everything after the dinner scene with his best friend and Michelle Pfeiffer, the ending just descended into tragedy-death-slop. Wasn’t an awesome movie.

I’m not sure why I’ve never really liked this movie. I wanted to give it another rewatch since it had been a while, and I’ve been on a bit of a movie binge lately. I wanted to see if my opinion had changed at all. It hasn’t. I don’t particularly like Tony’s character. I understand that he isn’t supposed to be a good person, and I appreciate other pieces of media that center around morally bad or complex characters. I enjoyed Breaking Bad and American Psycho. With Tony, however, I feel like he’s simply a stupid person, which makes his psychotic nature more frustrating and, to me, much less nuanced. The one redeeming quality I can give him is that he didn’t want to kill the two kids. Other than that, I just think he’s a genuinely terrible and unintelligent person. The only reason he gained power in the first place was by screwing over the other gangs, and I never felt like he was truly the untouchable drug kingpin the movie seemed to portray him as. From the beginning, he had the cops after him and constantly had people coming after him. Yes, he made a lot of money, but it didn’t last very long. In the end, it felt short lived. His downfall always felt inevitable. Overall, I understand the cultural importance of this movie, and there are definitely a few scenes that I really enjoyed. But even after another rewatch, I still found myself thinking why did this movie have to be three hours long? Lol. "All I have in this world is my balls and my word and I don't break them for no one." -Tony Montana

Today, after 32 years on this earth I am officially a man. That's how I should feel because when I was growing up this movie was mandatory to being a man. At least that's what it felt like. Everyone in highschool and college was obsessed with this movie, which I can understand if I was a teenager when it came out. Not a teenager 25-30 years later.  I remember going to friends houses and you would see the iconic movie poster on the wall, or a frame of him at the end of the movie. Quoting it constantly. Maybe it was the first "adult" movie they got to watch because their parents grew up with it, maybe it was their first exposure to hot women with their boobs out, the gangster life style, or the word "fuck" that wasn't said by their father to them.  It is interesting to me that so many men make this movie their whole entire personality, and if you are one of those people, you need help! I obviously never watched this movie as a child, or a teen. Chances are my parent's wouldn't have allowed me to. Then when I was old enough to seek it out, I just didn't care to. My only other exposure to the Scarface franchise besides what was said above was actually the video game for the Nintendo Wii. Why did I own this game at 12, I don't know but I did. I used to have to use the stupid joy con to drive around the little shitty cars in it. I never beat it, it was an open world GTA clone which is funny because Vice City is obviously a clone or heavily inspired by this film. I likely beat the first couple of missions and then drove around killing people. Anyways onto the actual film. A rags to riches to self destruction movie. Obviously a hugely influential movie, for all kinds of future work. I liked it for what it was but I felt that it did drag from time to time. I think from the 3rd act on the movie is extremely good. It really kicks into gear from the wedding on. Obviously the movie is most remembered from the epic conclusion which does live up to the hype. Al/Tony really carries this movie, I did find the movie kind of hokey and Al's over the top acting in majority of the stuff he does really fits the vibes of the movie. I am glad I watched it to finally say that I have but I don't see myself ever choosing to watch it again, and if I have kids someday this wouldn't be the top of the list of movies to show them. "I always tell the truth. Even when I lie." The best thing to come from this movie is the Bad Guy Razor Ramon

Segur que és una peli molt bona cinematogàficament i totes aquestes coses, també és una peli molt d’homes. Potser per això m’ha costat connectar. Això i l’encostipat terrible que portava. Crec que em vaig adormir al cine, soc una persona horrible. També em va semblar extrany que una persona no latina, fes de latina i fos el protagonista. Què dir? Pel·lícula dinàmica sobre l’American dream, l’ambició i que aunque la mona de viste de seda, mona se queda. Em va agradar quan va entrar la Michelle Pfeiffer, fàcilment la primera dona que surt. Entrada èpica. Crec que molt bon personatge i que se li podria haver tret més suc. Segurament podria dir més coses, però he trigat molt a fer la review i el meu cervell porta una bona època apagat. En fi, últimament estic molt trista i desconnectada i em costa apreciar l’art en general. Aviam com surt la següent.

The movie follows this very typical rise and fall formula you see done a lot in the crime genre but once Tony replaces Frank as the main guy it feels like the movie becomes far less interesting.

Yeah, it’s a little bit fucking ridiculous, and I think Pacino just has the tendency to go a little too big for my liking, but there are some great ideas in this politically. I read that Sidney Lumet was the original director and left as it turned too violent; man, I would love to see his version. I think De Palma’s Cheese Factor™ plays a bit better for me in the film Phantom of the Paradise , where camp is expected. I don’t love it here, as i find it too dissonant with the text of the narrative. Pacino sure is the guy to deliver it though, I found his performance mostly terrific.
